title: MLLP/TCP routes dropped from OpenHIM after Kafka integration
summary: Users found only HTTP and Kafka route types available; maintainers said MLLP/TCP were omitted after the Kafka work and offered unofficial interim images. Earlier users also could not set up or talk to TCP channels.

title: Runaway auto-retry that cannot be stopped
summary: Hundreds of failed batch transactions kept retrying every minute even with auto-retry disabled on the channel and after deleting the retry queue and restarting. Users need a reliable, visible kill switch for retry queues.
quote: I am still seeing hundreds of transactions being attempted

title: Transaction rerun/replay is buggy and loses lineage
summary: Reruns threw exceptions and left transactions stuck in 'processing', failed for public channels, and stopped linking parent/child transaction IDs. Replay must be robust and keep an audit link to the original.

title: Bulk/batch rerun of many transactions at once
summary: Operators asked to select a batch of failed transactions and queue them all for rerun rather than one at a time, with a background worker.

title: Restrict which users can see which transactions and message bodies
summary: Non-admin users tied to a client can see every client's transactions; users want visibility scoped per client/channel and a separate permission for viewing message bodies (PHI).

title: SSO via OIDC/Keycloak with role mapping
summary: Users want admin login through OIDC/SSO providers and to map IdP groups to engine permission groups instead of local passwords.

title: Granular role-based permissions in open-source engines
summary: Open-source Mirth forks lack user roles with specific permissions; users want to assign roles when creating users. OpenHIM users hit rerun permissions not enforced and channel methods not enforced.

title: TLS certificate changes require restart or crash the server
summary: New client TLS certs were not picked up until restart, and adding a new key/cert crashed core. Users want hot-reloadable certificates.

title: Certificate keystore and client trust by CA chain
summary: Large deployments with hundreds of point-of-care systems cannot register every client cert; users want a managed keystore and validation of clients against any cert in the chain or common root CAs.

title: Console login failures, often from clock skew or default-user setup
summary: Many users could not log in to the console: clock differences between servers broke auth, default root user failed on first docker-compose run, and the long 'Unable to login' thread collected dozens of reports.

title: Hex/control-character viewer for raw messages
summary: Analysts want to see hidden characters (CR, LF, VT/FS framing, non-ASCII) in the message viewer and optionally hex-escape them, because invisible bytes cause many HL7 failures.

title: Ambiguous status when some routes succeed and others fail
summary: A single transaction status string could not say whether the primary route succeeded while secondary routes failed; users asked for distinct completed vs failed semantics per route.

title: Per-step orchestration metrics and live flow visualizer
summary: Users wanted mediators to report custom metrics and orchestration steps into the transaction record, and a real-time visualizer of message flow across components.

title: Alerts on errored responses and scheduled reports that actually send
summary: Users asked for alerts when routes return errors and complained that daily/weekly reports were not delivered and reporting returned all zeros.

title: Channel matching and route editing are unintuitive
summary: Regex-based URL channel matching and an 'add route' button for editing an existing route confused users; they asked for simpler matching including HTTP method.

title: Chain mediators/processing steps without custom glue
summary: Users wanted to concatenate multiple mediators in one channel so the output of one feeds the next, instead of building orchestration mediators by hand.

title: Rate limiting on inbound channels
summary: Open question whether the HIM should rate-limit clients to protect downstream systems.

title: Message store grows unbounded; need retention by status
summary: Transaction collections took up a lot of space; Mirth-fork users want a separate, longer pruning window for errored messages than for successful ones, and teams build pruning as separate projects.

title: Configuration hard-wired to localhost and not externalizable
summary: Docker images fall back to localhost, Kafka broker not configurable, site config lives in the repo, JSON config lacks env-var substitution, and jpa.properties gets overridden. Users want 12-factor env-driven config.

title: MLLP listener/client errors cannot be caught; server stops accepting connections
summary: LLPException and port-in-use BindException cannot be caught by the caller, and SimpleServer stops managing new connections after two exceptions. Users need connection errors surfaced as handleable events with automatic recovery.

title: HAPI TestPanel (free HL7 test tool) broken on modern JREs, Linux and macOS
summary: The free desktop tool for sending/receiving test HL7 fails on non-Oracle JREs, Java 9+, Linux (hard OSX dependency), macOS installers and WebStart, and the latest version doesn't load messages. Analysts lack a maintained cross-platform HL7 send/receive/test tool.

title: Parsed HL7 object model uses ~60x the memory of the raw message
summary: A 30-50 KB ORU with 200 OBX took about 3 MB once parsed, making an in-memory queue of 10,000 messages impossible; users had to queue raw strings instead.
quote: the HAPI representation in memory is around 3 MB each!

title: MLLP over TLS drops connections or is missing
summary: HAPI's listener discards connections when TLS is enabled, and Node simple-hl7 has no TLS server at all, so users front engines with stunnel/haproxy.

title: TLS for every TCP connector should be built in, not a paid plugin
summary: The most-upvoted BridgeLink request is a bundled TLS plugin for all connector types; Mirth's SSL plugin is paid, pushing users to haproxy. In 2025 users consider TLS table stakes.
quote: Simply that in 2025, this should just be standard.

title: HL7 over HTTP transport support and spec ambiguities
summary: Vendors want to send HL7v2 over HTTP; users hit content-type questions, binary wrapper issues and a line-reading bug in HAPI's HL7-over-HTTP, and asked Node libraries to add an HTTP receiver.

title: Z-segments and custom message models are hard to access
summary: Getting a non-standard segment like ZBE throws or returns empty; custom model discovery broke between versions and Z-segment examples are missing.

title: OBX-5 'varies' type handling throws when OBX-2 missing or wrong
summary: Parsers throw or give misleading errors when OBX-2 doesn't declare the OBX-5 datatype, a common real-world defect; users want lenient parsing with a warning.

title: Message structures missing or mapped wrong across HL7 versions
summary: ADT_A04/ADT_AXX missing in some versions, NK1 not parsed for A01/A03, ORM event maps wrong, groups nested in groups fail, OBR column order differs from the 2.8.1 spec.

title: Validate HL7v2 against conformance profiles (NIST/IGAMT, Gazelle, local IGs)
summary: Users repeatedly ask how to validate messages against a version or implementation guide; nHapi lacks HAPI's conformance profile support, IPF wanted Gazelle IHE profiles for MLLP validation, and public-health pipelines bolt on NIST validators. NIST tools exist as JARs/web services but aren't integrated in engines.

title: Character encoding and escaping errors (umlauts, unicode, CR escaping, charset)
summary: German umlauts break conversion, unicode is garbled in the message API JSON, segment separators stopped being escaped, and HL7 charset (MSH-18) handling needed rework.

title: HL7v2 XML encoding round-trip failures
summary: XML parsing fails with multiple namespaces, GenericMessage can't encode to XML, and HAPI cannot re-parse XML it encoded itself.

title: Editors can't handle CR-only line endings used by HL7v2 files
summary: A long-running VS Code request for CR line-ending support is driven heavily by HL7 analysts and HL7 language-server authors; editing HL7 files outside an engine silently converts segment terminators.
quote: the lack of support of CR as end of line is killing that dream

title: Segment separator and line-ending tolerance in parsers
summary: Last segment without separator, newlines prefixed to segment names, missing 0x0d after MSH, and NiFi needing CR replaced with CRLF; parsers should accept CR, LF and CRLF.

title: FHIR rest-hook subscriptions unreliable (no indefinite retry, stuck 'requested', missed triggers)
summary: Rest-hook delivery gives up instead of retrying, subscriptions stay in requested state, most subscription pointcuts never fire, tag removals and :missing criteria don't trigger, and R5 sends notifications 19 times.

title: R5 topic-based subscriptions and websocket channels
summary: Users want R5/backport topic-based subscriptions with rest-hook, websocket, email and message channels; servers lag or fail on partitioned setups and Azure FHIR doesn't fire webhooks.

title: Subscription setup and debugging is opaque
summary: Implementers on chat.fhir.org get destination-unreachable with payloads, websocket connections that only receive keepalives, and no way to see why notifications don't arrive.

title: Publish FHIR change events to Kafka/NATS including deletes
summary: Teams stream FHIR resource changes to message brokers; delete events were missing and meta.source was inconsistently populated in Kafka messages.

title: Multi-tenant isolation leaks (subscriptions and search across partitions)
summary: Non-cross-partition subscriptions match resources in other partitions, conditional URLs have cross-tenant impact, and multi-tenant support was a top request.

title: Bulk FHIR $import immature and $export has size/ID problems
summary: Bulk import doesn't work on HAPI starter, IBM lacked deletion markers for _since exports, export hits unexpected size limits, and moving data between servers requires rewriting references.

title: Bulk data client: retries, attachments and silent parameter drops
summary: Downloads aren't retried, EAGAIN is fatal, Binary references and DocumentReference attachments aren't handled, and a malformed _since is silently dropped.

title: FHIR batch/transaction bundle support gaps
summary: Batch and transaction POSTs were missing, PATCH in bundles unsupported, and _cascade=delete/$expunge ignored inside transactions; engines pushing converted bundles depend on these.

title: Framework/runtime upgrade treadmill (Spring Boot, Jakarta, Java versions)
summary: The most-reacted HAPI FHIR and IPF issues are requests to support new Spring Boot/Jakarta versions as old ones go EOL; Java baseline changes broke users. Healthcare teams want long support windows and low-dependency runtimes.

title: Vulnerable transitive dependencies with slow fixes
summary: Scanners flag CVEs via transitive deps (fhir.core, lodash.set, Postgres JDBC, Node base images); users ask for fix timelines, and Mirth-fork users ask whether CISA-reported CVEs are fixed.

title: OAuth2/SMART authorization configuration for FHIR endpoints
summary: Users want optional, documented OAuth/SMART configuration and fine-grained authorization out of the box rather than writing interceptors.

title: Standards-based audit trail (AuditEvent/ATNA) with reliable writes
summary: Users want FHIR AuditEvent or IHE ATNA output, counts of all resources returned, XUA-compliant client auditing, and a decision on whether failed audit writes should fail the request or be async.

title: Horizontal scaling: several nodes on one database, cluster-aware schedulers
summary: Users asked how to run multiple servers against a single DB and inject clustered scheduler config; Medplum agent users need two agents on one host handled gracefully.

title: Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry tracing
summary: Users want a /metrics endpoint for Prometheus and OpenTelemetry traces so the engine fits existing monitoring.

title: Store large binaries/attachments in S3-compatible object storage
summary: Large binaries in the database become unretrievable or bloat it; users want S3/MinIO-backed storage for binaries and bulk files.

title: Hard payload size limits reject real CCDs and documents
summary: The converter service rejects CCDA input over 100 KB/512 KB and multi-MB DocumentReferences; customers' CCDs routinely exceed that and they want a configurable limit.

title: Container images, Helm charts and OS packages for deployment
summary: Users repeatedly ask for official Docker images, docker-compose for the full stack, Helm charts, RPMs and tar/zip bundles; existing images are inconsistent with releases.

title: Running multiple FHIR versions; R5 breaks deployments
summary: Switching the latest Docker image to R5 fails to start, upgrades break R5 beans, and users want R4 and R5 side by side.

title: Encrypt stored health data at rest
summary: Users asked how to encrypt resource content stored in the database tables rather than relying on disk encryption.

title: v2-to-FHIR converters mishandle repeating segments, fields and groups
summary: Only the first PR1 became a Procedure, PID-11/PID-13 repeats were collapsed, and ORU messages with nested repeating ORC/OBR/OBX groups were hard to map; values went missing silently.

title: Off-by-one field numbering around MSH-1/MSH-2
summary: Tools counted MSH fields one off (encoding characters not counted as fields) and miscounted CX components, confusing analysts mapping by field number.

title: Default v2-to-FHIR maps skip commonly sent fields and segments
summary: Out-of-box templates dropped race/ethnicity, PV1-41, EVN, IN1 to Coverage, SPM/Specimen, MSH/MessageHeader and patient identifiers; users had to fork templates for basics.

title: Converters support only a handful of message types
summary: SIU, OMS and ADT A06/A07 not supported; one converter handled only four v2 messages. Each new event type means new mapping work from scratch.

title: Converted FHIR output fails validation
summary: Generated datetimes lack timezones, DiagnosticReport.status and Immunization fields are missing, ICD-10 system URLs invalid, quantities emitted as strings, SN comparators and TQ times produce invalid FHIR. Users want output validated against profiles in the pipeline.

title: Stateful conversion: match ADT updates to existing patients/encounters
summary: Stateless converters emit new resources per message; users asked how an A03 updates the encounter an A01 created, how MRNs are matched, and for transaction/conditional bundles instead of collections.

title: Mapping templates are hard to author and debug
summary: Liquid templates are hard to debug and format, need helpers just to set a variable, JEXL in YAML only exposes one utility class, and the VS Code extension context menu is flaky.

title: Mapping DSLs lack basic functions (casts, math, now, max)
summary: Users of Whistle repeatedly asked how to convert string to number and back, do math, get the current timestamp, and take the max of a list; a full general-purpose language would avoid this.

title: Terminology mapping: local codes, custom code systems, ConceptMaps
summary: Users need to add custom coding systems, fix deprecated code system URIs, apply ConceptMaps (including to OMOP), handle SNOMED licensing, and map local v2 codes that have no FHIR equivalent; the v2-to-FHIR IG leaves local codes to implementers.

title: Converter build and deployment friction
summary: Azure-only deployment templates fail validation, builds break on macOS/M1 and Linux, NuGet dependencies disappeared, Docker image versions are undiscoverable, and Whistle won't build. Users want a single binary/container that runs anywhere.

title: Data lineage on converted resources
summary: Users want every generated resource to carry where it came from (source message, control ID, template) via meta.source or lineage extensions, valid per FHIR.

title: Unknown throughput limits; need load-test baselines
summary: Users with 100k-message bursts asked about template evaluation performance and thread safety; a state hub found its ceiling only through its own load testing of the engine.

title: Open-source healthcare integration projects go dormant
summary: Users repeatedly ask if projects are dead, what the roadmap is, or whether a branch is still maintained; adopting healthcare tooling feels risky when vendors abandon it.

title: Reliable ACK handling and recovery in Node HL7 clients
summary: Node HL7 clients get stuck awaiting ACK with no recovery, crash on ECONNRESET, can't send ACKs back to devices, and can't time out a connect attempt.

title: Repetition and component access APIs are wrong or missing
summary: getComponent ignores repetitions, tilde handling is unclear, Terser/Visitor can't read repeated fields, and NiFi's attribute extraction ignored repeats.

title: HL7 batch files (FHS/BHS) and multiple messages per stream
summary: Users needed to process HL7 batch messages and multiple messages on one connection.

title: TypeScript types for HL7 libraries
summary: Node developers asked for TypeScript declarations for the HL7 message API.

title: Parsers hang or throw on malformed input instead of erroring cleanly
summary: Bad inputs caused unhandled exceptions and permanent hangs, undefined segments stopped the app, X12 parsers returned the next segment's value instead of null, and GenericMessage encoding threw ClassCastException.

title: ACK the sender only after the message is durably stored
summary: Agents dropped messages from their queue once forwarded even if the server died before processing; the device never got a response. Users want end-to-end confirmation, durable queues and retries, and ACK-failure never silent.

title: Configurable behavior on NACK: halt FIFO on AR vs continue/retry on AE
summary: Users want per-channel control of whether an application reject halts the queue (strict ordering) or is skipped, separate from retry-able application errors; one adapter didn't NACK invalid messages at all.

title: Return a custom ACK/NACK when a script errors and still log the error
summary: When a handler throws, users lose either the ability to respond to the HL7 sender or the error propagation; they want both for graceful handling and debugging.

title: Throttle concurrency to avoid overloading downstream systems
summary: With 100+ channels running in parallel, target HL7 systems get overloaded; users want simple settings like running grouped channels in sequence with a delay or max concurrency per queue, not engineer-heavy workarounds.

title: On-prem edge agent install and lifecycle is rough
summary: Hybrid cloud engines rely on an on-prem agent; users hit installers that skip required values, can't update settings after install, hard-coded service values, no checksums, no tray status, and agents requiring endpoints they don't need.

title: Push outbound messages through the edge agent, sync or async
summary: Users needed cloud-to-on-prem push that opens outbound connections from the agent and supports 'prefer async' so callers aren't blocked.

title: Failed/NACKed message payload not visible in logs
summary: Logs record only message size and ACK/NACK, not the payload or error detail, and logs vanish with the pod; users can't find which message failed.

title: Cloud-vendor MLLP bridges add auth/PubSub friction and lock-in
summary: Users struggled with default credentials, PubSub permissions, single-direction adapters and Azure-only templates; they want the same engine on-prem and in any cloud.

title: Version history, rollback and Git integration for channels and code
summary: The top OIE request is channel and code-template history with rollback and remote repo sync; BridgeLink users want the history plugin pre-installed, global scripts in the repo, and GitLab PAT support that actually works.

title: Native unit and automated testing of interfaces
summary: Automated testing of channels is a long-standing unmet wish; the community is still listing workarounds. Converter users asked for an end-to-end test harness too.
quote: A long standing quest for Mirth users has been automated testing

title: Hung script readers fail silently for weeks
summary: A JavaScript reader stuck in 'Reading' stopped polling for 30+ days unnoticed; users want per-connector script timeouts that raise errors, since flow-based external monitoring can't tell stuck from busy.
quote: I want an error, not a silent failure.

title: Shared libraries should declare which channels use them, not vice versa
summary: Libraries must be edited every time a new channel uses them, exports are hard to share, cloned channels lose their library dependencies, and the dependency window is hard to search.

title: Cancel a long-running message search
summary: Analysts searching daily by accession number etc. can't cancel a slow search once started.

title: Modern, scalable admin UI (dark mode, HiDPI, no freezes)
summary: The Swing administrator looks dated, doesn't scale on large screens, has no dark mode, and freezes or stops refreshing over time.

title: Admin client requires launchers/JNLP instead of a browser
summary: Managing the engine needs a separate Java launcher that breaks across versions; the community debated which launchers to recommend and replacing the server launcher.

title: Password rules enforced only in the client
summary: Password policy was checked by an optional client call and not enforced on user creation; legacy weak hashes still accepted.

title: Upgrades between versions and with plugins break
summary: Point upgrades error out, plugins break across upgrades, variable names changed without documentation, the Windows installer behaves badly, and plugin migration converters fall behind releases.

title: Transformer error stores the original message as the 'transformed' one
summary: When a transformer throws, the stored transformed message is the untransformed input, misleading anyone inspecting or reprocessing it.

title: White-label branding for resellers
summary: Integrators reselling the engine want centralized control of product name, logos and support links, or removal of branding.

title: Stable plugin API decoupled from engine releases
summary: Plugins are tied to a specific engine release; developers want a separate versioned API and documented plugin install/management.

title: Paid add-ons and license changes in 'open source' engines
summary: Implementers note the engine was free but features like SSL were paid, and Mirth went closed-source at 4.6, prompting forks; buyers are wary of open-core bait-and-switch.

title: Rule builder and event viewer usability gaps
summary: Users asked for case-insensitive comparisons in the rule builder and searching events by predefined types.

title: DICOM Modality Worklist and DICOM routing in the engine
summary: Users want DICOM worklist (MWL) support in the HL7 engine, and imaging teams keep building their own DICOM routers.

title: DICOM forwarding needs persistent queue, retry and routing by called AE
summary: Orthanc users asked for a send queue with retry; Lua routing runs before the instance is fully stored and suits only basic cases, and the TODO lists missing retry counters.

title: File writer: write header row on file creation
summary: Delimited file outputs need a header written once when a file is created, not per message.

title: HTTP listener and API tuning (header size, gzip, new methods)
summary: Users asked for configurable request header size on HTTP listeners, gzip on the admin API, and HTTP QUERY support.

title: Config map keys with dots silently fail to expand
summary: Environment config keys containing dots silently don't substitute into connector fields, so a channel runs with a literal placeholder.

title: Human-readable rendering of lab messages
summary: Dense HL7/FHIR lab messages need a report-style visualizer so analysts and clinicians can read results without decoding segments.

title: Receiver-specific HL7 requirements cause rejections
summary: Each state receiver demands different fields and formats (ORC-23, OBX-23 truncation to 50 chars, MSH-4, OBR-25/OBX-11, OBX-23.6); messages fail until per-receiver transforms are added. Long threads show this is the bulk of routing work.

title: Partner onboarding is slow, manual and ticket-driven
summary: Onboarding each sender or receiver takes long threads: validating test files, setting up connections, building receiver settings and documenting requirements. New EHR vendors and IG version bumps trigger the same cycle.

title: Duplicate submissions and excessive result floods
summary: Receivers got duplicate submissions after failures and excessive numbers of results from uploads; deduplication/idempotency is needed at the engine.

title: Targeted resend of a date range or subset after a fix
summary: After fixing a mapping (e.g. missing ordering provider), teams must resend everything since a date to one receiver, resubmit corrected data, and chase last-mile failures.

title: Content-level data quality rules with clear error messages
summary: Structurally valid messages still carry future specimen dates, 'Unknown' names, malformed accession numbers, missing LOINC or collection dates; business-rule validation sometimes returned no error message at all.

title: Search and dashboards by business keys (facility, lab, CLIA), not just IDs
summary: Operators asked to put facility name, testing lab and CLIA into logs and to have progress dashboards and validator summaries per feed.

title: Self-service validation of test files for senders
summary: Instead of emailing files back and forth, senders want an upload/validate UI that reports what's wrong before go-live.

title: Last-mile delivery failures and connection discrepancies go unnoticed
summary: Deliveries to receivers fail at the final hop (SFTP/DB writes) and counts disagree between sender and receiver; long threads to reconcile what arrived.

title: Transform behavior is under-documented
summary: Teams needed better documentation of transforms and asked how specific datatypes (email XTN) should translate.

title: Production-like test data without PHI
summary: Realistic testing needs real traffic, but it contains PHI (including in Z-segments and employer names); manual scrubbing is error-prone and replacements must stay consistent across a patient's messages. Generic samples miss workflow and volume issues.

title: Regression testing by replaying captured traffic and diffing old vs new output
summary: Interface teams want to capture a fixed message set, run it through old and new versions, and get field-level diffs on deploy or upgrade; today this is hand-built per engine or via small CLI diff tools.

title: v2-to-FHIR has no generic solution; mappings are per supplier and hand-coded
summary: chat.fhir.org implementers find no generic converter: each feed needs its own mapping, mostly hand-written code on top of an engine, and the HL7 v2-to-FHIR IG is incomplete below the component level.

title: Convert by message structure, not trigger event
summary: Implementers argued converters should key off message structure (ADT_A01 shared by A01/A04/A08/A13) so one map covers many events.

title: A maintained Node.js-native HL7v2/FHIR conversion engine
summary: Implementers chose the neglected Handlebars converter only because it ran on Node; there is demand for a supported Node/JS engine for v2 and FHIR.

title: FHIR Mapping Language/StructureMap tooling is immature
summary: Few implementations beyond the Java reference, a tutorial with technical errors, known spec gaps in chaining, and implementers stuck constructing targets.

title: C-CDA parsing and conversion is brittle
summary: Vendor heterogeneity and errors in C-CDA limit interoperability; converters crash on sections without template IDs, emit invalid JSON for half the files, or drop resources, and 100% fidelity is considered unrealistic.

title: FHIR to C-CDA (reverse) mapping
summary: Users asked whether mapping engines support FHIR input producing CCDA output.

title: No mature open-source X12 EDI support in integration engines
summary: X12 libraries are narrow or stalled: users question a Node X12 project's future, hit wrong values, parallel-processing crashes, incomplete schemas, and Python 3 import errors; NiFi users want X12 to other formats. Engines handle 837/835/270/271 via custom code.

title: X12 acknowledgments (999/TA1) and repeating HL loops
summary: Users needed TA1/999 acknowledgment handling and parsing of repeating HL hierarchical loops.

title: IHE XDS/PIX/PDQ actors with paging, hardened XML and current profiles
summary: IHE users want ITI-18 queries with sorting/paging, XDS target communities, working PDQm queries, and XML processing hardened against XXE/SSRF.

title: TEFCA/QHIN exchange: XCPD/XCA, patient matching and CDA ingestion
summary: Joining a QHIN doesn't make a system interoperable: teams must run IHE cross-community endpoints, handle probabilistic patient discovery, and reconcile retrieved CDA into workflows, with FHIR exchange phased in later.

title: MLLP framing implementations are fragile
summary: Frames split across TCP buffers broke decoding, ACK reads didn't drain the buffer, the MLLP decoder leaked memory, multiple MLLP components threw ConcurrentModificationException, and a Go reader could drop data.

title: NiFi has no MLLP listener with ACKs
summary: ListenTCP can't receive and acknowledge HL7, so users write custom processors; HL7 attribute extraction has encoding and repetition issues.

title: Timezone and fractional-second handling in HL7 datetimes
summary: Date helpers converted to server local time, dropped timezone, misread offsets and fractional seconds, or under-padded milliseconds.

title: Identifier normalization (SSN, assigning authority, IDs with spaces)
summary: SSNs kept dashes, assigning authorities became bogus references, IDs with spaces produced invalid FHIR, and a version upgrade removed identifier type text users relied on.

title: Mapping output changes silently between versions
summary: Upgrades altered Patient identifiers, a PID fix removed all other resources from bundles, and variable names changed without notice; users need output regression checks on upgrade.

title: Kafka/NATS backbone with TLS and exactly-once delivery
summary: Healthcare integration stacks built on Kafka/NATS needed TLS, exactly-once delivery, reliable consumers, and configurable brokers.

title: One ingestion API that validates and converts HL7v2, C-CDA, CSV and FHIR
summary: A state HIE built separate engine channels to expose $validate and bundle endpoints for HL7v2, CCDA, CSV and FHIR plus an HTTP endpoint for HL7v2; they want one multi-format validate-and-convert front door.

title: Promote channels between environments with environment-specific settings
summary: Teams want site config kept out of the code repo, template deployment from a separate repo, and channel migrations between environments without hand edits.

title: Engines become shadow app platforms because deploys elsewhere are slow
summary: Teams put business logic in the interface engine because it's the only fast way to ship; engines need governance and testing to match that role.

title: Interface specs and message samples derived from real traffic
summary: Generic samples tell you nothing about a specific interface; analysts want system-specific samples and machine-readable profiles (IGAMT-style) generated from observed traffic to document and test interfaces.

title: FHIRcast support with STU3 hub URLs
summary: Users integrating with third-party FHIRcast hubs needed STU3-style topic URLs.

title: Opt-in usage telemetry to steer open-source roadmap
summary: Maintainers lack data on running installations and feature use; community debated anonymous opt-in telemetry.
